note: Real answers from Jupiter's keyless prediction API, captured by scripts/capture-jupiter.mjs --events and served back to the publisher template's own client by internal/jupiter's tests. `path` is the request as the template sends it, parameters and all, so a change to what it asks for fails a test instead of quietly testing something else.

cases.name: events-first
cases.description: The first page of a filtered listing, with more to come.

cases.name: events-second
cases.description: The second page of the same walk.

cases.name: events-empty
cases.description: A page past the end: no events, and `hasNext` false, which is what stops a walk.

cases.name: events-bad-parameter
cases.description: A category the provider does not have. Its answer names the parameter, and lists the categories it does have — which is where this template's own list came from.

cases.name: market-closed
cases.description: A market that has closed and settled. It is one of September's Bitcoin price markets, so it stays settled: what it is a fixture for is the shape of a closure.

cases.name: market-missing
cases.description: A market that does not exist. `code` is what tells this apart from any other 404.

cases.name: market-open
cases.description: A market read directly, as a reconciliation reads one: the same market the first page lists, asked about on its own.
